title: Renewal risk dial-in prep — Amelia Chen (AE-CSM 1:1)
body:
Meeting: AE/CSM sync for PendoHealth renewal (60m)
Date: 2026-03-11 10:00 PT (prep notes timestamped)
Attendees (planned): Amelia Chen (AE), Samir Patel (CSM), Ravi Kumar (SE optional), Lena Ortiz (Customer Success Manager - shadow)
Objective: Align on top risks ahead of renewal (2026-04-15), agree outreach cadence, and lock a remediation + value plan we can present in exec renewal meeting on 2026-03-18.

Quick summary / context (one-paragraph):
PendoHealth (enterprise, healthcare analytics) was an early Redwood Dedicated customer. Usage growth stalled last 2 quarters; tokens/month down ~28% QoQ. Main triggers: (1) integration latency spikes during nightly batch inference (last incident: 2026-02-22, ~3 hours degraded throughput), (2) PO org change — previous champion (Dir. Data) left Jan 2026, new sponsor (VP Product) is less technical and focused on cost. Contract up for renewal 2026-04-15, estimated ARR $1.2M. Support NPS trending down in last 45 days (ticket backlog + missing runbooks).

Why this is at-risk:
- Usage decline + exec sponsor change increases churn probability
- Latency incidents hit analytics SLAs (customer cited missed reports)
- Finance flagged cost escalation after Q4 run-up (unplanned burst costs)
- No clear adoption plan for features we released (embedding rerank)

Primary goals for this call:
1) Agree triage and short-term mitigation plan for latency (ops + SE owners).
2) Define a 30/60/90 day adoption plan to show measurable value (eng + product asks).
3) Prepare a 1-page renewal proposal (AE owns pricing anchor + concessions) and an exec briefing deck for 3/18.

Notes / important facts to reference in meeting:
- Last incident: 2026-02-22 (ticket #JIRA-ACCT-7890) — root cause: autoscaler misconfig combined with a non-restartable legacy job. Ops fix applied 2/23 but customer wants SLO guarantee and RCA doc.
- Billing spike in Dec 2025 driven by unbatched inference jobs from their nightly pipeline (see billing PDF sent 2026-01-06).
- Existing committed capacity: 4x A100-style instances, they've been bursting to 7x on peak nights.
- Champion change: Sarah Lin (Dir. Data) -> Marcus DeVries (VP Product). Marcus is conservative on vendor expansion and requests 2x cost-savings targets.
- Renewal window: formal notice required by 2026-03-31 to keep current pricing.

Suggested agenda (30-40m sync + 20m action planning):
- 0-5m: Quick framing + roles (who will lead exec meeting)
- 5-20m: Technical risk review (Ravi to summarize ops RCA + quick wins)
- 20-35m: Adoption plan (Samir + Amelia propose 30/60/90 milestones and metrics)
- 35-50m: Commercial ask (Amelia presents pricing anchor and concession options)
- 50-60m: Assign actions, timelines, prep for 3/18 exec briefing

Suggested talking points for exec meeting (3/18):
- Top line: Redwood supports PendoHealth production inference at X qps and Y average latency; we own the remediation and propose runbook + SLA addendum.
- Cost narrative: seasonal burst in Dec caused short-term overage; propose committed cushion + burst cap (model: dedicated reserve + auto-fallback to lower-cost variant).
- Value narrative: show 3 use-cases where Redwood reduced runtime for their end-customer pipelines and tie to revenue (e.g., monthly reporting window shortened by 40% during pilot).
- Ask: 12-month renewal with 10% price uplift tied to service level and usage floor. Offer 90-day technical commitment and playbook.

Red flags to surface explicitly:
- Customer is asking about migrating to another provider for cost (mentioned in sales call 2026-03-03).
- Execs are asking for a one-week rollback option post-renewal (red flag: means lack of confidence).

Probing questions for Marcus (VP Product) during exec meeting:
- What are 2 measurable outcomes you need from Redwood in the next 90 days to feel confident renewing?
- How much variability in peak nights is acceptable from a cost perspective? Do you prefer committed pricing or predictable monthlies?
- Are there internal timelines tied to investor/board reporting that we need to sync to?

Proposed 30/60/90 adoption plan (high-level):
- 30d: Stabilize nightly pipeline (ops patch + KV cache warmers), provide RCA doc, and run daily health reports. Success metric: zero severe incidents for 14 consecutive days.
- 60d: Enable embedding rerank on 20% of traffic, measure lift and latency. Success metric: +8% model-driven KPI and <150ms P95.
- 90d: Expand rerank to 60% and launch dashboard for product leaders showing business metrics. Success metric: executive sign-off that feature maps to a revenue or ops metric.

Action items (explicit, owners, due):
- Amelia: Draft renewal pricing options + draft concession table (due 2026-03-13).
- Samir: Create 1-page adoption playbook with measurable milestones and dashboards to present 3/18 (due 2026-03-15).
- Ravi: Deliver ops RCA doc + list of recommended runtime changes (autoscaler tweaks, batch-window guardrails) and quick patch for nightly job (due 2026-03-12).
- Lena: Coordinate with customer PM to lock exec meeting timing, gather Marcus' top-2 outcomes (due 2026-03-12).
- Amelia + Samir: Rehearsal run for exec briefing (30m dry-run) on 2026-03-17.
- Ops on-call (cc ops-rotation@redwood): Implement temporary burst cap and notify billing team to flag any >10% daily spend (ops task, due 2026-03-11).

Email snippet (to send to Marcus after internal alignment):
"Marcus — following our sync, we'd like to propose a short remediation plan and a renewal conversation on 3/18. Key asks: 1) technical commitment to stabilize nightly jobs within 30 days, 2) adoption plan to demonstrate measurable value in 60 days, 3) a renewal with a committed baseline to avoid burst surprises. We'll share a 1-page summary + exec deck by 3/15. Can you confirm 3/18 availability?"

Potential concessions to consider (priority order):
- Short-term: 90-day price protection and one operational review call per week.
- Mid-term: Discounted committed cushion for first 6 months (limit: 15% of ARR).
- Long-term: Custom SLA addendum for latency with financial credits if not met (only if legal approves).

Notes to self / heuristics:
- Keep concessions tied to measurable commitments (30/60/90) to avoid open-ended discounts.
- Use RCA doc + ops checklist as the proof of work — executives respond to concrete operational artifacts.
- Avoid promising refunds; prefer credits and operational commitments.

Open questions to resolve before 3/15:
- Can finance approve a temporary committed cushion discount up to 15%? (Ping: Nadia in finance)
- Legal: timeline to sign SLA addendum (estimate 3 weeks) — is that fast enough for 4/15 renewal?
- Product: do we have a safefall model for rerank quantization that keeps latency under 150ms P95? (Ping: model-onboarding team)

Attachments to prepare and share:
- 1-page renewal summary (Amelia)
- Exec briefing deck draft (Amelia + Samir)
- Ops RCA doc (Ravi)
- Billing breakdown (Samir + finance extract)

Follow-up schedule after 3/11 sync:
- 3/12: Ops RCA complete (Ravi) + Lena confirms Marcus availability.
- 3/13: Amelia shares pricing anchor + concession memo.
- 3/15: Full deck and 1-pager ready for review.
- 3/17: Dry-run rehearsal.
- 3/18: Exec renewal briefing.

Quick scratchpad (random notes):
- If Marcus pushes for cost-free migration window, escalate to RSM (Jason) — do not agree without legal sign-off.
- Consider offering a short trial of Redwood Optimize recommendations (free assessment) to show immediate cost-saving potential — Ops + Optimize team can support.
- Bring up success story: "HealthCo East" case study where we reduced nightly window by 35% (use as comparison).

Last-minute prep checklist (15 minutes before exec call):
- Slide 1: One-line problem statement + ask (Amelia)
- Slide 2: Ops remediation summary + timeline (Ravi)
- Slide 3: 30/60/90 adoption metrics (Samir)
- Slide 4: Commercial anchor + concessions (Amelia)
- Slide 5: Next steps + decision request

End of notes.

(If time after sync: draft the Marcus email and attach 1-pager; keep copy in /shared_drives/company/memos for audit)
